findings.title: Login IDP cache not invalidated when organization enabled or public broker status changes
findings.body: The new cache for getForLogin stores the set of IDP internal IDs based only on the IDP model's own fields (enabled, linkOnly, hideOnLogin, organizationId, and BROKER_PUBLIC config). However, the actual login availability of an organization-linked IDP also depends on the organization's enabled state and potentially on organization-level public broker settings. The invalidation logic (registerIDPLoginInvalidation and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) only reacts to IdentityProviderStorageProvider CRUD operations and does not invalidate the login cache when an organization is disabled/enabled or its public broker flag changes. As a result, after such an organization change, the cached list will still contain the affected IDPs, causing getForLogin to return IDPs that are no longer suitable for login. Downstream consumers that rely on the returned stream without re-checking isEnabled() will present stale login options.

findings.title: Cleanup attempts to remove a hardcoded 'alias' instead of the actual IDP alias
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup call `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` uses the literal string "alias" instead of the variable `alias` holding the actual IDP alias. This means the cleanup will try to delete an identity provider with alias "alias" (which does not exist), leaving the created IDPs in the realm after the test. This can pollute subsequent tests or cause cleanup failures. The same mistake appears on line 425 as well.
